title: Nut-Free Toasted Marshmallow Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft vanilla cupcakes topped with fluffy marshmallow frosting, torched golden in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a campfire treat in cake form. I made a batch for my son's nut-free classroom party and the golden toasted swirls disappeared first. The base is a simple vanilla cupcake, soft and moist, with no nuts anywhere in the ingredient list. The real star is the marshmallow frosting, whipped fluffy then toasted lightly with a kitchen torch or broiler. Toasting the frosting gives it a light graham cracker color and a faint caramel smell. It only takes a few seconds per cupcake, so watch closely. This recipe is safe for nut-free school events and easy enough for a weeknight bake. Kids love helping toast the tops under supervision.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each. Stir in vanilla extract.
Add flour mix and milk in three additions, alternating and mixing just until combined.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely on a wire rack.
For frosting, whisk egg whites, sugar, and cream of tartar in a heatproof bowl set over simmering water until sugar dissolves, about 3 minutes.
Remove from heat and beat with a mixer on high until stiff, glossy peaks form, 5 to 7 minutes. Beat in vanilla.
Pipe frosting high onto cooled cupcakes using a large open star tip.
Toast the frosting lightly with a kitchen torch, moving in slow circles until golden. If no torch, broil cupcakes on the top rack for 30 to 60 seconds, watching closely.
tips: Keep the torch moving so the frosting toasts evenly without burning.
If using a broiler, freeze frosted cupcakes for 10 minutes first so the cake does not overheat.
Make the frosting right before piping. It loses volume if it sits too long.
Double check all packaged ingredients for a nut-free label if serving at school events.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes without a kitchen torch?
faq.answer: Yes, use your oven broiler on high. Place frosted cupcakes on the top rack for 30 to 60 seconds and watch the whole time.

faq.question: Why did my marshmallow frosting deflate after toasting?
faq.answer: This happens if the frosting sits too long before use or gets too warm under the torch. Pipe and toast within an hour of making it.

faq.question: Are these cupcakes safe for a nut-free classroom?
faq.answer: Yes, none of the ingredients contain nuts. Always check your specific brands for cross contamination warnings before sending them to school.

faq.question: Can I make the frosting ahead of time?
faq.answer: It is best made fresh since it loses its fluffy texture in the fridge. You can bake the cupcakes a day ahead and frost them right before serving.

conclusion: These cupcakes bring a fun bakery trick home with simple ingredients. Toast the frosting slowly and you get a soft cake with a golden marshmallow top every time.
